claude.sample_unit: hand conditions (each generating patient education materials per model and prompt)

links.outcome: Share of AI-generated patient education materials at or below sixth-grade reading level
links.effect: Question 1: neither model produced any PEMs at or below sixth-grade level. Question 2: ChatGPT 3.5 produced none; ChatGPT 4.0 produced 28% at or below sixth-grade level (P < .001).
links.quote: Our study shows neither ChatGPT 3.5 nor 4.0 could produce responses at the recommended sixth-grade reading level.

links.outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education materials relative to plain-language targets
links.effect: ChatGPT 3.5 Flesch Kincaid Grade 12.20 and ChatGPT 4.0 5.49 on question 2; neither version generated more than 50% of responses at an acceptable reading level.
links.quote: However, neither version generated more than 50% of responses at an acceptable reading level, regardless of a priming phase beforehand.

links.outcome: Change in readability with priming example text and prompt variation
links.effect: Priming improved ChatGPT 4.0 (Flesch Kincaid 6.58 vs 5.49, P < .0001) but worsened ChatGPT 3.5 (8.07 vs 12.20, P < .0001).
links.quote: Conversely, ChatGPT 4.0’s performance significantly improved when primed with an example text at a sixth-grade reading level.

unlisted_practices: Priming LLM with a sample text at the target reading level to improve output readability

links.effect: After priming, ChatGPT 4.0 produced 28% at/below sixth grade; ChatGPT 3.5 produced none (P < .001).

unlisted_practices: Priming ChatGPT with an example sixth-grade text and explicitly requesting sixth-grade patient education materials.
